queries: TypeScript import declaration semantics merging named imports side effect order AST safe consolidation 2026

sources.title: TypeScript organizeImports.ts (microsoft/TypeScript)
sources.technique: the compiler's own import-organization service: merges same-module named imports, preserves side-effect imports
sources.limits: full service; V155 implements a narrow safe subset

sources.title: Merge driver: imports merge per name; side-effect imports kept in moved positions
sources.technique: side-effect imports execute the module for side effects ⇒ never reorder/merge; keep in position

sources.title: Normalise import blocks (18/48 modules import the same specifier twice)
sources.technique: same-specifier duplicate imports are common; consolidation is a real need

findings.statement: Merging two NAMED imports of the SAME specifier is runtime-safe: an ES module is evaluated once at its FIRST import position regardless; consolidating the named bindings into the first occurrence does not change module-evaluation order.
findings.appliedInV155: consolidate ONLY same-specifier named-only groups; place the merged import at the FIRST occurrence; refuse if a side-effect import of any module sits between group members.

findings.statement: Value imports of DIFFERENT specifiers must NOT be reordered/merged (changes ESM evaluation order); side-effect imports must be kept in position; namespace/default/attribute/type imports have distinct semantics.
findings.appliedInV155: hard refusals: different specifier / default / namespace / side-effect / alias / type-only / import-attributes / attached-comment / name-collision / non-contiguous group / malformed — NATIVE_REFUSED with a precise reason.

findings.statement: The TS compiler's own organizeImports merges same-module imports but preserves side-effect ordering — the authoritative safety model.
findings.appliedInV155: V155 implements a NARROW, provable subset of that model (contiguous same-specifier named-only), refusing everything it cannot prove safe (SafeRepair 'never a wrong patch').

honesty: Reference techniques; V155 implements only the demonstrably-safe subset at the syntactic tier (no type-checker). No paid API/credential/external write. €0 clients.
